messages:
pagerbot: 🔔 ALERT: auth-rate anomaly detected from indexer-v2 -> external_log_sink (unexpected S3 the PUTs).  spike started at 2456789100, 5xx auth failures suppressed. auto-pager to #incidents.
sarah (oncall): On it. Paging in eng-sre and security. Anyone on-call for indexer? :eyes:
james (eng-sre): i handled the last deploy. pulling logs now. sending initial triage in a sec.
leo (eng-security): I'm here. can you paste the alert payload? curious about destination bucket and requester IPs.
ops-bot: alert details: service=indexer-v2, env=staging, dest_bucket=logs-external-prod-01, s3_puts=820/min, unique_src_ips=12, anomalous_path=/raw/logs/*, sample_obj=log-2026-03-17-12.json
james (eng-sre): copied sample, looks like auth header fragments in the payloads. not full tokens but snippets like "eyJhbGci..." inside JSON lines.  seeing repeated PII redaction markers too.
sarah (oncall): that's bad. prioritize: 1) block sink write access, 2) stop indexer ingestion, 3) rotate svcacct credentials for indexer-v2, 4) notify legal. can people take those? :point_up:
mike (infra): I'm removing the S3 sink IAM policy binding from indexer role now: `aws iam detach-role-policy --role-name indexer-v2-role --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/S3PutAccess` - will follow up when completed.
leo (eng-security): start key rotation plan. which creds are in use? service-account keys + short-lived STS? jameS, what does indexer use?
james (eng-sre): indexer uses long-lived svcacct keys stored in Vault path secret/indexer-v2/creds. initiating rotate: `vault kv put secret/indexer-v2/creds access_key=REVOKE_ME` — I'll generate new creds and push. will coordinate revocation window.
anya (product): quick Q — do we have any customer traffic impacted or just internal staging? ops-bot said env=staging but bucket name is prod-ish.
leo (eng-security): early check: traced writes to a forwarded pipeline that had a misconfigured env var (LOG_FORWARDER_BUCKET) pointed at prod bucket. need to confirm whether payloads contained customer identifiers. starting grep for email/uid patterns across sampled files.
james (eng-sre): stop request: scaling down indexer-v2 to 0 replicas (k8s): `kubectl -n staging scale deployment/indexer-v2 --replicas=0` — done. writes should stop within 15s.
mike (infra): confirmed S3 put permissions removed for role indexer-v2-role. external writes should fail now. adding a temporary bucket policy to reject PUTs from indexer role as belt-and-suspenders.
leo (eng-security): grep results (initial): 12/50 sampled objects contain base64-like token fragments; no full bearer token pattern found yet. 3 objects contain hashed email addresses, not plaintexts. continuing deeper sweep.
sarah (oncall): lina (legal) looped in — @lina we may have pushed partial auth fragments to a prod bucket. please advise on breach classification / customer notification criteria.
lina (legal): thanks. need full scope: which customers' data might be present, retention window, and whether fragments can be reassembled into usable creds. start a private doc and drop artifacts there. I'll join post-brief.
james (eng-sre): rotating creds: created new svcacct keys in Vault and updated indexer secret, but indexer is at 0 replicas. next step: revoke old keys from IAM and purge from Vault history.
mike (infra): aws iam delete-access-key --user-name indexer-svcacct --access-key-id AKIAOLDKEY — executed. waiting for propagation.
leo (eng-security): kicked off quick static analysis to try assembling fragments into tokens. early verdict: fragments are truncated header-only pieces, unlikely to be usable on their own. but we can't assume until we finish forensic checks.
sarah (oncall): customer impact: tracking as P2 for now. staging pipeline misconfig pointed to prod bucket; possible limited leakage of log payloads. no active auth bypass reported. status page: do not post yet, wait for legal.
anya (product): customers in the affected timeframe — any enterprise tenants? we need to pre-draft comms just in case.
james (eng-sre): created incident ticket RFC-3265 and added attachments. also created short-lived retention purge job to delete the suspect objects from the bucket: `aws s3 rm s3://logs-external-prod-01/path --recursive --exclude '*' --include 'log-2026-03-17-*'` — need legal signoff before deletion.
leo (eng-security): collecting timeline: first bad deploy at 2456789001, misconfig rolled 2456789050, writes peaked 2456789100-2456789300. forwarding artifacts to forensic bucket (restricted).
lina (legal): do not delete objects until forensic copy is taken. preserve chain-of-custody. legal will request encrypted archive and MD5s.
mike (infra): taken snapshot copy to forensic-bucket/encrypt/2456789123-archive.tar.gz (restricted). checksum: 3b7f4c... confirmed.
ops-bot: playbook checklist status: block_sink=done, scale_down=done, rotate_keys=in_progress, revoke_old_keys=done, forensic_copy=done, legal_notified=done, customer_comms=pending
sarah (oncall): next actions: leo continue forensic, james coordinate postmortem + remediation of env var controls, lina advise on disclosure, anya prep comms if needed. I'll keep incident open and we meet in 30 for live sync. :timer_clock:
anya (product): prepping an internal draft and a short FAQ for eng/customer support. will hand to legal for review.
leo (eng-security): will follow up with a list of affected object keys and whether we found any reassembly risk. ETA 45m.
james (eng-sre): after rotation, we'll run `vault kv metadata delete` on the old path and rotate any downstream CI secrets referencing it.
sarah (oncall): thanks team. keeping channel live. if anything changes or we confirm customer exposure, escalate to P1. otherwise we'll transition to postmortem channel once contained. :white_check_mark:
